meta.purpose: A.7e — NEGATIVE CONTROL for the T3 channel-context trigger. A.7d reports T3's catch rate on adversarial fixtures; on its own that number is uninformative, because T3 was measured against a context object carrying exactly the properties T3 was built to detect. This file supplies the other half: legitimate chats that deliberately SHARE funnel properties and must not be accused.
meta.provenance: SYNTHETIC. These context objects and message texts were written by the project team to model real, benign chat patterns. They are not captured from real chats — labelled exactly as A.7d's adversarial context object is labelled, and for the same reason.
meta.labelling_rule: Every entry is legitimate by construction. The target is therefore ZERO false `absent`. `shares_funnel_property` records which property of the documented scam funnel each one deliberately shares, so no entry can be dismissed as an easy negative.
meta.sharpest_case: registered_ra_premium_signals — securities content, funnel-shaped group name, AND a registration that resolves. If T3 causes an accusation there, channel context is overriding a valid credential, which inverts the architecture. Treated as P0.
meta.sender_note: `sender` is the identity CLAIMING the registration, which is the poster — never the chat title. Passing a group name as the poster identity makes a genuine registrant's number score as a name mismatch and produces a spurious `collision`. For the two fixtures whose credential must resolve, `sender` is the literal string {name}, substituted at eval time with the real registrant drawn from the SEBI register.
